arxiv-1706-03388.title: Quantifying statistical uncertainty in the attribution of human influence on severe weather
arxiv-1706-03388.creator: Christopher J. Paciorek
arxiv-1706-03388.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Christopher J. Paciorek. Event attribution in the context of climate change seeks to understand the role of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions on extreme weather events, either specific events or classes of events. A common approach to event attribution uses climate model output under factual (real-world) and counterfactual (world that might have been without anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions) scenarios to estimate the probabilities of the event of interest under the two scenarios. Event attribution is then quantified by the ratio of the two probabilities.

arxiv-2305-02341.title: Failure of Topological Invariants in Strongly Correlated Matter
arxiv-2305-02341.creator: Jinchao Zhao, Peizhi Mai, Barry Bradlyn and Philip Phillips
arxiv-2305-02341.description: Abstract We show exactly that standard ‘invariants’ advocated to define topology for non-interacting systems deviate strongly from the Hall conductance whenever the excitation spectrum contains zeros of the single-particle Green function, G G , as in general strongly correlated systems.

arxiv-2306-12509.title: Joint Prompt Optimization of Stacked LLMs using Variational Inference
arxiv-2306-12509.creator: Alessandro Sordoni Xingdi Yuan Marc-Alexandre Côté Matheus Pereira, Adam Trischler Ziang Xiao Arian Hosseini Friederike Niedtner Nicolas Le Roux, Microsoft Research Montréal
arxiv-2306-12509.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can be seen as atomic units of computation mapping sequences to a distribution over sequences. Thus, they can be seen as stochastic language layers in a language network, where the learnable parameters are the natural language prompts at each layer.

arxiv-2310-20475.title: Linked Papers With Code: The Latest in Machine Learning as an RDF Knowledge Graph
arxiv-2310-20475.creator: Michael Färber, David Lamprecht
arxiv-2310-20475.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce Linked Papers With Code (LPWC), an RDF knowledge graph that provides comprehensive, current information about almost 400,000 machine learning publications. This includes the tasks addressed, the datasets utilized, the methods implemented, and the evaluations conducted, along with their results.

arxiv-2401-04388.title: Using gravitational waves to see the first second of the Universe
arxiv-2401-04388.creator: Rishav Roshan and Graham White
arxiv-2401-04388.description: Abstract Gravitational waves are a unique probe of the early Universe, as the Universe is transparent to gravitational radiation right back to the end of inflation. In this article, we summarise detection prospects and the wide scope of primordial events that could lead to a detectable stochastic gravitational wave background.

arxiv-2404-19307.title: Enhancing GUI Exploration Coverage of Android Apps with Deep Link-Integrated Monkey
arxiv-2404-19307.creator: Han Hu, Han Wang, Ruiqi Dong, Xiao Chen, Chunyang Chen
arxiv-2404-19307.description: Abstract . Mobile apps are ubiquitous in our daily lives for supporting different tasks such as reading and chatting. Despite the availability of many GUI testing tools, app testers still struggle with low testing code coverage due to tools frequently getting stuck in loops or overlooking activities with concealed entries.

arxiv-2405-09332.title: Revealing the Production Mechanism of High-Energy Neutrinos from NGC 1068
arxiv-2405-09332.creator: Abhishek Das, B. Theodore Zhang, Kohta Murase
arxiv-2405-09332.description: Abstract The detection of high-energy neutrino signals from the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 provides us with an opportunity to study nonthermal processes near the center of supermassive black holes. Using the IceCube and latest Fermi -LAT data, we present general multimessenger constraints on the energetics of cosmic rays and the size of neutrino emission regions.

arxiv-2410-13553.title: SynapticRAG: Enhancing Temporal Memory Retrieval in Large Language Models through Synaptic Mechanisms
arxiv-2410-13553.creator: Yuki Hou, Haruki Tamoto, Qinghua Zhao, Homei Miyashita
arxiv-2410-13553.description: Abstract Existing retrieval methods in Large Language Models show degradation in accuracy when handling temporally distributed conversations, primarily due to their reliance on simple similarity-based retrieval. Unlike existing memory retrieval methods that rely solely on semantic similarity, we propose SynapticRAG, which uniquely combines temporal association triggers with biologically-inspired synaptic propagation mechanisms.

arxiv-2506-06362.title: CR-BLEA: Contrastive Ranking for Adaptive Resource Allocation in Bilevel Evolutionary Algorithms
arxiv-2506-06362.creator: Dejun Xu, Jijia Chen, Gary G. Yen, Min Jiang
arxiv-2506-06362.description: Abstract Bilevel optimization poses a significant computational challenge due to its nested structure, where each upper-level candidate solution requires solving a corresponding lower-level problem. While evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are effective at navigating such complex landscapes, their high resource demands remain a key bottleneck—particularly the redundant evaluation of numerous unpromising lower-level tasks.

arxiv-2507-18993.title: Agent0: Leveraging LLM Agents to Discover Multi-value Features from Text for Enhanced Recommendations
arxiv-2507-18993.creator: Blaž Škrlj, Benoît Guilleminot, Andraž Tori
arxiv-2507-18993.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) and their associated agent-based frameworks have significantly advanced automated information extraction, a critical component of modern recommender systems. While these multitask frameworks are widely used in code generation, their application in data-centric research is still largely untapped.

arxiv-2508-17429.title: Out-of-plane angle resolved second harmonic Hall analysis in perpendicular magnetic anisotropy systems
arxiv-2508-17429.creator: Akanksha Chouhan, Abhishek Erram, Ashwin A. Tulapurkar
arxiv-2508-17429.description: Abstract Second Harmonic Hall (SHH) measurement is a standard and well accepted technique to estimate spin orbit torque (SOT) efficiencies in perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) systems. Generally, field sweep and in-plane angle sweep SHH measurements are performed and SOT efficiency calculation is done using effective fields based formalism.

pmc-10670393.title: A Review on Motor Imagery with Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation: Bridging Motor and Cognitive Welfare for Patient Rehabilitation
pmc-10670393.creator: Rosary Yuting Lim, Kai Keng Ang, Effie Chew, Cuntai Guan, Clara Casco
pmc-10670393.description: Research has shown the effectiveness of motor imagery in patient motor rehabilitation. Transcranial electrical stimulation has also demonstrated to improve patient motor and non-motor performance. However, mixed findings from motor imagery studies that involved transcranial electrical stimulation suggest that current experimental protocols can be further improved towards a unified design for consistent and effective results.

pmc-11505542.title: Role of Tail Dynamics on the Climbing Performance of Gecko-Inspired Robots: A Simulation and Experimental Study
pmc-11505542.creator: Shengchang Fang, Guisong Chen, Tong Liu, Weimian Zhou, Yucheng Wang, Xiaojie Wang, Stanislav N Gorb, Giuseppe Carbone, Peter Fratzl, Thomas Speck
pmc-11505542.description: Geckos are renowned for their exceptional climbing abilities, enabled by their specialized feet with hairy toes that attach to surfaces using van der Waals forces. Inspired by these capabilities, various gecko-like robots have been developed for high-risk applications, such as search and rescue.

pmc-11656381.title: TIHI Toolkit: A Peak Finder and Analyzer for Spectroscopic Data
pmc-11656381.creator: Kyunghoon Han, Ariadni Boziki, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Joshua T Berryman
pmc-11656381.description: Complex signal vectors, particularly spectra, are integral to many scientific domains. Interpreting these signals often involves decomposing them into contributions from independent components and subtraction or deconvolution of the channel and instrument noise. Despite the fundamental nature of this task, researchers frequently rely on costly commercial tools.

pmc-12370815.title: Subjective workload in operating room team members during robotic hernia procedures
pmc-12370815.creator: Daphne Remulla, Cammy Tang, Kimberly P Woo, William C Bennett, Alvaro Carvalho, Brianna L Slatnick, Kimberly S Miles, Benjamin T Miller, Lucas R Beffa, David M Krpata, Ajita S Prabhu, Clayton C Petro
pmc-12370815.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). While robotic surgery has been dominated by a single platform in the United States for over 25 years, the introduction of new robotic systems may have an impact on subjective workload. Therefore, we aimed to establish baseline workload measurements for operating room team members using the DaVinci surgical robot during robotic hernia procedures, providing reference points for evaluating team adaptation as new robotic platforms are introduced.

pmc-12422905.title: Proteomics reveals periodontitis-driven oxidative stress and lipid metabolism disruption in NAFLD
pmc-12422905.creator: Boyuan Sun, Xiaomeng Liu, Yixuan Jiang, ShuangYan Qi, Zhengyu Guan, Hongjiao Li
pmc-12422905.description: BackgroundPeriodontitis is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Oxidative stress and lipid metabolism dysregulation may serve as key pathological links. This study investigates the impact of periodontitis on NAFLD progression and identifies molecular targets involved in hepatic oxidative stress and lipid alterations.

pmc-12542197.title: Ssrp governs germline development independent of the FACT complex in Drosophila spermatogenesis
pmc-12542197.creator: Xiaoning Tan, Yuhan Lou, Zhiyong Yin, Jiaqi Zhao, Jia Wang, Jichen Jin, Yunbo Wang, Yongmei Xi, Xiaohang Yang, Huimei Zheng
pmc-12542197.description: BackgroundThe heterodimeric FACT complex (SSRP1/Ssrp and SUPT16H/Dre4) is primarily recognized as a chromatin remodeler. While mutations in this complex are linked to human intellectual disability and it maintains neural stem cell fate in flies, single-cell RNA sequencing reveals robust FACT complex expression in human testicular germ cells. Nevertheless, its specific functions during spermatogenesis remain unexplored.

pmc-12782601.title: Clinical Decision-Making Case: A Giant Headache
pmc-12782601.creator: Mark Portman, Linda Herman
pmc-12782601.description: AudienceThis certifying exam practice case is intended for emergency medicine residents and medical students rotating through emergency medicine.IntroductionGiant cell arteritis (also known as GCA, temporal arteritis, cranial arteritis, or Horton’s disease) is the most common systemic vasculitis.1 Patients commonly present with a new and unique headache, often with tenderness in the temporal region.

pmc-13263664.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis versus open reduction and internal fixation in treatment of trimalleolar ankle fractures: A propensity-matched TriNetX database study
pmc-13263664.creator: Ronak J Mahatme, Meredith Murphy, Shawn A Moore, Anish Gangavaram, Caroline Szabo, Abraar Huq, Richard Laughlin
pmc-13263664.description: BackgroundTrimalleolar ankle fractures are complex injuries associated with high complication rates and poorer outcomes, particularly in elderly and medically comorbid patients. While open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) remains the standard treatment, alternative strategies such as tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis (TTCA) have been increasingly explored for high-risk populations.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was performed using the TriNetX Research Network.

uslaw-usc-t42-s1395cc7.title: 42 U.S.C. § 1395cc–7 — Extension of Acute Hospital Care at Home initiative
uslaw-usc-t42-s1395cc7.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s1395cc7.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 7 (Social Security); Subchapter XVIII (Health Insurance For Aged And Disabled); Part E (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general (1) Extension With respect to inpatient hospital admissions occurring during the period beginning on the first day after the end of the emergency period described in section 1320b–5(g)(1)(B).
